reviews.review: ArmA III itself is a good game, I'm not going to deny that. But as time has dragged out, this game has just become more and more bloated with DLCs, ones that are honestly fairly small, and lackluster, in my own opinion, and continue to charge nearly the price of the full game for each of these DLC's. This game is increasingly becoming a cash grab, and I get they're trying to keep the community alive, but releasing $20-40 DLC every now and then is NOT the way to keep a game alive. Adding up all the DLC's and factoring in the cost of the base game? Almost $170 USD. A lot of servers will let you play without having the DLC's, but, of course, this being the cash grab it is, is made nearly unplayable due to the game physically not letting you interact with anything from any of the DLC's other than instantly pulling up a storage page to purchase it whilst in-game. This game is six years old at this point, and with how forced some of these DLC's are, it's NOT worth $170 USD. Save your money.

If you're into military games I highly recommend ARMA III.
The game manages to strike a pretty perfect balance between realism and fun; you can expect to find aiming difficult if you've been sprinting around, you won't be doing any bunnyhopping, and you won't be pulling off 360 noscope headshot BS...but the game still offers cinematic combat and fun scripted sequences.
If you're tired of the heavy liberties BF and COD take with realism, you will find this game very refreshing.

Also of note is the wonderful scenario editor, in which you can play with making your own missions. These can be as simple or complex as you like, and don't require a heavy knowledge of scripting (though developing a knowledge of the code will let you make some very cool missions). The only limit is your imagination.
